messages:
Priya (oncall): incident-bot fired ~3m ago for inference pool us-west-2, continuous-batcher growth + multiple OOMKills
incident-bot: severity: P1 | service: inference-serving | started: 1710551123
Priya (oncall): I'm triaging, seeing batcher.accumulator climb steadily for model rdx-gpt-3-small-prefetch, several pods restarted with exit code 137
Lee (eng-runtime): that model had the reorder patch recently. last week Canary showed a minor accumulator drift but not this magnitude
Sam (eng-sre): customer-facing alerts incoming — p95 latency up 6x, 504s reported. 3 nodes have pod restarts and kubelet evictions
Alex (support): we have a ticket from acme-inc describing chat RPCs timing out at ~15s, asking for ETA
Marta (customer-success): looping in their SREs. they want immediate mitigation steps :worried:
Priya (oncall): quick log extract:
```
[2026-03-15T20:12:03Z] batcher: enqueue req id=abc123 size=1
[2026-03-15T20:12:04Z] batcher: accumulator.size=640
[2026-03-15T20:12:04Z] prefetch: miss ctx=ctx-xyz
[2026-03-15T20:12:05Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed 24.8GB -> cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2026-03-15T20:12:05Z] process: SIGKILL (OOM)
```
Lee (eng-runtime): matches prefetch miss + unbounded accumulator. hypothesis: prefetch attach not cleared on prefetch timeout when reorder enabled
Priya (oncall): reproducing in staging with synthetic long-prefix traffic and `runtime.prefetch.reorder=true` — accumulator grows unbounded
Lee (eng-runtime): fast mitigations:
- flip flag runtime.prefetch.enabled=false for the pool
- reduce REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX to 32
- scale replicas +25% to drain backlog
- cordon the flappy hosts
Priya (oncall): applying flag via control plane API -> 200 OK. patching env var REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX -> rolling
Sam (eng-sre): cordoning node ip-10-0-45-7, draining. set autoscaler min to current to avoid scale-down
incident-bot: escalation messages silenced for this incident
Alex (support): told Acme we'll apply temporary mitigations (prefetch disabled, smaller batches). ETA 2-3min to see improvement
Lee (eng-runtime): after flag flip accumulator decaying, batch sizes back to ~15, no OOMs for 2m
Priya (oncall): GPU usage: before ~99% -> after ~60% on recovered nodes
Marta (customer-success): Acme acknowledged improvement. requesting postmortem
Lee (eng-runtime): root cause plan: add per-request lifecycle logging (enqueue/attach/detach/commit) and guard to evict attachments older than 30s
Priya (oncall): proposing hotfix runtime:v2026.03.15-evict-old to force-evict attachments >30s; canary 10% first
Sam (eng-sre): will monitor rollouts, alert if OOM >3 in 5m or node.evictions spike
Priya (oncall): starting canary rollout -> image patched, 10% canary
Alex (support): offered temporary org-level rate limit to Acme, they accepted
Marta (customer-success): scheduling postmortem call after fix PR lands
Lee (eng-runtime): also adding exponential backoff for prefetch retries in next PR
Priya (oncall): handoff notes for next shift:
- monitor batch.accumulator.size and gpu.memory.used
- eng-runtime to land PR for eviction guard + backoff + test
- eng-sre to keep cordoned nodes as needed
- support to update customers
Sam (eng-sre): leaving monitoring checklist: OOMKills, batcher.accumulator.growth, inference.latency.p95, node.eviction.count
Priya (oncall): canary healthy; p95 trending down. keeping ticket open for RCA and postmortem
Alex (support): Acme confirms service normal, requested postmortem
Marta (customer-success): I'll handle the customer call
Lee (eng-runtime): assigning PR to myself, will add regression test
Priya (oncall): handing off to evening oncall @Sam. logging timeline and commands in incident doc
Sam (eng-sre): ack, will watch overnight. ping me if hotfix rolls to 100%
Priya (oncall): thanks all, closing live thread but incident doc remains open for follow-ups.
